eng_desc: Students who pass this course will have similar English skills to those students who satisfy the English Proficiency requirement. eng_desc: Students will study and practice the skills of Western and contemporary Thai style choral singing, explore the feature of melodic lines arranged with 2-part and 4-part harmony, and the connection between music and its social change in each period.

eng_desc: Students will study the development of Western music from the past to the present, as well as major forms and categories. eng_name: Western Solo Singing: Theory and Practice 2

derived_eng_desc1: Focuses on Mon music theory and practical skills in playing instruments for public performance.

eng_name: Music in Thai Drama and Dance

eng_desc: Students will study theories and skills of listening to various forms of intervals and chords. The exercises include immediate transcription of both melody and rhythm, as well as singing with the correct pitches.

eng_desc: The artistic concepts and forms related to the social, cultural, religious, economic, and political contexts of of Thailand. Field studies will be included.
derived_eng_desc1: Explores artistic concepts, forms, and cultural contexts of Thai art history.

eng_desc: The artistic concepts and forms related to the social, cultural, religious, economic, and political contexts of the mainland Southeast Asian countries, such as Cambodia, Vietnam, Myanmar, Indonesia, and Malaysia, from ancient times to the present. Field studies will be included in this subject.
derived_eng_desc1: Covers artistic concepts, forms, and cultural contexts of Southeast Asian art history.

eng_desc: The background, forms, concepts, aesthetic principles, and creative techniques in art and ceramic artists in the field of pottery vessels. Creating ceramic art from local materials and understanding the problems and processes in developing the work.
derived_eng_desc1: Focuses on creative techniques, aesthetic principles, and processes of pottery and ceramic art.

eng_desc: The basic skill painting with water color and acrylic from objects and models in order to convey visual; express imagination in way of creative painting. The colour theory, colour properties, colour circles, pigmentary primaries, and values such as monochrome, harmony, colour tone; psychological effects on colour perception; colour creation in various designs.
derived_eng_desc1: Teaches painting skills, color theory, and creative expression through various art designs.

eng_desc: The basic use of lines, line control in different directions, holding a pencil. Skills in using the tools are also required. (To pass this subject, the students must achieve at S or A score of 60 percent)
derived_eng_desc1: Teaches fundamental drawing skills, including lines, shapes, forms, light, and shadow.

eng_desc: The concepts and the norms of traditional Thai court arts and local Thai artistic wisdom. The philosophy behind the creativity, the related customs, the technical processes, materials and the training of each artistic discipline.
derived_eng_desc1: Explores traditional Thai artistic wisdom, court arts, philosophy, and creative processes.

eng_desc: The content covers the origin and the formation of the stream of World Music as a major musical category distinguished from Western Classic, Pop and Rock from the US, as well as the history of Root Music and World Beat which are the result of the hybridization between Pop, Rock, and local musical styles from various countries. It also includes the background, the significance, the style, and the development of World Music, as well as the relation to economics, social and political contexts. The areas are music from Asia, Africa, Europe, North America, and South America, as well as the cross-genre between World Music and other music styles.
derived_eng_desc1: Explores the origin, history, styles, and development of World Music, including its social and political contexts.

eng_desc: The content of this subject covers various fields of aesthetics, particularly of music. derived_eng_desc1: Covers various fields of aesthetics, particularly in music, exploring beauty, creativity, and styles across historical periods.

eng_desc: The course investigates aesthetic and fundamental elements of art and built environment. These include appreciation in value and meaning, analyses and criticisms, and connections to lives and social contexts.
derived_eng_desc1: Investigates aesthetic elements of art and built environment, focusing on appreciation and criticism.

eng_desc: The course is designed to study and perform works of screen printing. The technique and process of mold-making as well as water linseed and oil linseed printing are also studied. The student will keep practicing finding creative ways to be relevant to screen-printing techniques.
derived_eng_desc1: Focuses on screen printing, mold-making, and creative techniques in art.

eng_desc: The creation of sculptures using ceramic techniques and materials involves preparing the clay body for sculptural work, decorating, firing, and controlling the pieces to achieve the intended conceptual outcome. The process includes glazing and decorating the sculptures, as well as addressing and solving any issues that arise during the creation process. This is done through various artistic ideas and styles, utilizing ceramic methods and techniques to develop the sculptures according to the design concept.
derived_eng_desc1: Focuses on creating ceramic sculptures using artistic techniques, materials, and design concepts.

eng_desc: The cultural context and wisdom of people in the community, along with information related to the roots of traditional knowledge, local wisdom, ways of thinking, methods, and forms of handicraft art. The factors, conditions, context, and cultural objects, as well as techniques and steps in creating artwork. Exploring and understanding the design of handicraft products, integrating contemporary wisdom with accumulated traditional knowledge (includes field study).
derived_eng_desc1: Explores cultural context, traditional knowledge, local wisdom, and handicraft art design.

eng_desc: The development of Britain through the various eras that characterized what was a tumultuous century both at home and abroad, beginning with the Edwardian period of the early 1900s.
derived_eng_desc1: Focuses on the development of Britain through various historical eras.

eng_desc: The development of artistic concepts and forms in Europe from the beginning to the present day, the relationship and influence between art and politics, economics, society, religion, as well as the influence of the East on Western artists. Field studies will be included.
derived_eng_desc1: Explores the development of Western artistic concepts, forms, and their societal influences.

eng_desc: The development of ceramics in the history of humanity, according to the civilizations and cultures of the world, includes the forms and contexts related to the ideas behind the creation of ceramics throughout different historical periods. derived_eng_desc1: Explores the historical development of ceramic styles, forms, and cultural impacts.

eng_desc: The emergence and development of cultures and societies, arts and sciences, local wisdoms, and economic systems of Northern communities in Thailand and neighboring countries; the kingdoms' prosperity, the decline of Lanna dynasties, the consolidated as a tributary state, as well as the socio-cultural management for restoring Lanna's glory, and local development.
derived_eng_desc1: Focuses on the emergence and development of Lanna cultures, societies, arts, history, and socio-cultural management.

eng_name: Ethnicity and Identity in British and American Literature

derived_eng_desc1: Focuses on ethnic and racial dilemmas in British and American literature, exploring representations of ethnicity and identity.

eng_desc: The evolution of art and architecture in South East Asia and Thailand from the Sukhothai and Rattanakosin periods to the present. Cultural and technological influences from the neighbours on the development of Thai art and architecture are explored. Discussion also includes analysis of unique building styles that reveal diverse lifestyles of people in the past.
derived_eng_desc1: Focuses on the evolution and appreciation of Thai art and architecture, cultural influences, and building styles.

eng_name: Thai Art and Architecture Appreciation for Interior Design
eng_desc: The evolution of art and interior architecture in Southeast Asia and Thailand from the Sukhothai and Rattanakosin periods to the present. Cultural and technological influences from the neighbours on the development of Thai art and interior architecture. Analysis of unique building styles that reveal diverse lifestyles of people in the past.
derived_eng_desc1: Focuses on the evolution and appreciation of Thai art and interior architecture, cultural influences, and building styles.

eng_desc: The evolution of design from the past to the present time. The context and conditions relevant to the process of thinking and synthesizing a designed product. The influence of various periods (Renaissance, the Age of Enlightenment and the Industrial Revolution), major art and crafts movements and the formation of guilds. The outcome and the discourse of thinkers and product designers in the Thai socio-cultural contexts, on both a national and local scale, are also included, as well as the chronology of evolution and the major influential designers.
derived_eng_desc1: Focuses on the evolution of design, its socio-cultural contexts, historical periods, art movements, and influential designers.

eng_desc: The evolution of human design from the past to the present, including the contexts and conditions that have influenced the thinking and synthesis of human design work. The impact of discoveries during the Renaissance, ideas in the Age of Enlightenment, the Industrial Revolution in Europe, movements in art and craftsmanship, guild associations, and the incidents and discourses of thinkers and designers in Western, Eastern, and Thai cultures. The chronological development of design work and examples of influential designs that have driven change or innovation in society.
derived_eng_desc1: Focuses on the evolution of human design, historical contexts, cultural influences, art movements, and influential designers.

eng_desc: The foundation of three-dimensional figure design, as well as learn the related visual elements (line, form, mass-volume, space, texture, light and shadow) and the connection to the rule of perspective. The lessons will be based on various materials, as well as on major works from creative three- dimensional designs.
derived_eng_desc1: Focuses on the foundation of three-dimensional figure design, visual elements, perspective, materials, and creative design works.

eng_desc: The fundamental of fashion design and fashion products design process materials technique and apparel categorization based on the occasion and target group.
derived_eng_desc1: Focuses on the fundamentals of fashion design, product design process, materials, techniques, and apparel categorization.

eng_desc: The history and concept of conservation. Theory and practice in conservation relating to museum and cultural heritage. Management of museum collections and archive materials. Knowledge of technology applications for museum and heritage studies. Development of students' understandings and skills in conservation practice for museum and heritage management.
derived_eng_desc1: Focuses on conservation, museum collections, and cultural heritage, aligning with cultural and creative expression.

eng_desc: The history and development of art, culture, and society in Lanna focuses on the relationship between art and its various contexts, which influenced the development and creation of artworks in the Lanna region. It examines the cultivation and learning process through the transmission of artistic styles (style) in craftsmanship, techniques, beliefs, customs, and practices that reflect the unique and regional characteristics in Lanna art. The study highlights how these elements impact the creation of contemporary Lanna art and design (with field studies).
derived_eng_desc1: Directly focuses on Lanna art, design, culture, and artistic styles, aligning with cultural and creative expression.

eng_desc: The history and development of museums and concepts in museum studies. Definition of museum and its role in contemporary society. Basic knowledge regarding museum management, collection management, storytelling, exhibition design, and museum ethics.
derived_eng_desc1: Focuses on museum studies, management, collections, and exhibition design, related to cultural institutions.

eng_name: Britain and the United States in Southeast Asia
eng_desc: The history of Thailand and Southeast Asia's interactions with the Western World, especially the United States and Britain, beginning with the age of colonialism to the present day.
derived_eng_desc1: Directly focuses on the history of international interactions, aligning with the history component of arts and humanities.

eng_desc: The history of Western thought from the Pre-socratics to the philosophers of the Hellenistic period. The course will focus on the philosophies of Heraclitus, Parmenides, Socrates, Plato, Aristotle and the Stoics.
derived_eng_desc1: Directly focuses on Western philosophy and philosophers, aligning with the philosophy component of arts and humanities.

eng_desc: The history of artfocusing on major periods of artistic development; the changing relationship between art and society.
derived_eng_desc1: Directly focuses on the history of art and artistic development, aligning with the arts component of arts and humanities.

eng_desc: The important role of material cultures in the movement of religions. Interactions between people and objects in the context of religions, and religious movement along trade. The legacy and role of material cultures in the living of present-day local communities in the areas where religions established themselves.
derived_eng_desc1: Focuses on religion, material cultures, and their interactions, aligning with the religion component of arts and humanities.

eng_desc: The meaning and major concepts of philosophy, e.g. God, truth, goodness, beauty; debates and questions in subfields of philosophy, e.g. metaphysics, epistemology, ethics, aesthetics, logics; the relations between philosophy, religion and theology.
derived_eng_desc1: Directly focuses on major concepts and subfields of philosophy, aligning with arts and humanities.

eng_desc: The meaning, roles, and functions of fashion and clothing, as well as the relationship between fashion and clothing with social, economic, political, and cultural contexts. The evolution of fashion and clothing at the global and Thai levels, the relationship between fashion and textiles, various design concepts in fashion design.
derived_eng_desc1: Focuses on fashion, clothing, design concepts, and cultural contexts, aligning with creative expression.

eng_desc: The modernist movement in British and American literature; the complex relationship between modernist and postmodernist literary forms.
derived_eng_desc1: Focuses on modernist and postmodernist literature, aligning with languages and literature in humanities.

eng_desc: The origin and development of both tangible and intangible cultural heritage, forms, past issues, as well as concepts in preservation, from both cultural and international perspectives, and the utilization of cultural heritage for economic benefit. Studying prominent case studies at both national and international levels.
derived_eng_desc1: Covers cultural heritage, its preservation, and utilization from cultural and international perspectives, fitting humanities.

eng_desc: The political, social and cultural framework of the visual arts in Britain and the United States, including the relationship between fine art and architecture.
derived_eng_desc1: Focuses on British and American visual arts, fine art, and architecture within cultural frameworks.

eng_desc: The principle elements of visual art design composition. The students will be trained to analyze the essence of each visual element and its existence in nature, as well as to synthesize their own creativity as a ground for further visual art and design concept.
derived_eng_desc1: Focuses on principles of visual art design composition, visual elements, and creative synthesis.

eng_desc: The principles and processes involved in basic printmaking include the use of materials and tools to create print artworks. This involves designing and creating printing plates and printing images using various techniques such as mono print, paper block print, woodcut print, collagraph, silk screen print, and etching. These methods are then applied in design work for further creative development.
derived_eng_desc1: Covers basic printmaking principles, processes, techniques (woodcut, silkscreen, etching), and creative development.

eng_desc: The principles of basic weaving techniques, practice hand weaving, warp and weft preparation, structure and pattern design and planning. Field trips included.
derived_eng_desc1: Covers weaving techniques, textile design, and pattern creation, aligning with arts and design.

eng_desc: The process and concepts of basic design, the development of creative thinking through the methods of substitution and transformation of forms, development of ideas by studying nature, and synthesis through linking imagination and issues to form a conceptual approach, ideas, themes, and meaning in accordance with the design objectives. Analyzing examples of quality design works in terms of both functionality and aesthetics. (To pass this subject, students must achieve at least a C grade)
derived_eng_desc1: Explores basic design concepts, creative thinking, form transformation, and aesthetic analysis of design works.

eng_desc: The process and the concept of basic design. Creative thinking in interpreting shapes and forms. The learning is based on surveying nature, and focuses on synthesizing one's concept, idea and theme in connection with his/her imagination and designated issues. Moreover, the design outcome must cohere with the designated objective. The exercises include the analysis of any selected quality design work both for its functionality and aesthetics. (To pass this subject, the students must achieve at least 2.0 or C grade.)
derived_eng_desc1: Covers basic design concepts, creative thinking, form interpretation, and analysis of design functionality and aesthetics.

eng_desc: The process of designing and creating costume, accessories, and make up for various types of performance, especially for non-realistic performance according to students' interests under the instructor's supervision.
derived_eng_desc1: Focuses on designing and creating costumes, accessories, and makeup for various types of performances.

eng_desc: The process of furniture design is introduced. Materials and techniques for making prototype-furniture which include joinery and finishing techniques are covered.
derived_eng_desc1: Introduces furniture design, materials, techniques, joinery, and finishing for prototype creation.

eng_name: Forming Techniques from Fiber and Fabric Material
eng_desc: The properties of various types of fibers, basic stitching techniques, and 3D shaping using textile materials and fibers from various techniques allow for creative manipulation of fibers. This process utilizes the properties of materials, basic tools, technologies, and innovations to shape fibers creatively and apply them in design work.
derived_eng_desc1: Covers forming techniques from fiber and fabric materials, 3D shaping, and creative application in design.

eng_desc: The relationship between people and cultural objects and visual perception, based on the concepts of material culture and visual culture, explores issues related to the body, art, commodities, and consumption, media and new technologies, collecting objects and museum exhibitions.
derived_eng_desc1: Explores material and visual culture, examining cultural objects, visual perception, art, and media.

eng_desc: The role of contemporary performing arts in society. The movement of contemporary performing arts both in Thailand and internationally. Analyzing case studies from various countries to identify strengths and limitations of the movement in shaping social spaces for performing arts. Global trends in performing arts. External studies will be conducted.
derived_eng_desc1: Focuses on contemporary performing arts and their societal role, directly fitting arts and humanities.

eng_desc: The role of the curator in driving art in society. Analyzing the societal aspects related to art and curation. Concepts and principles in determining the core ideas of exhibitions and art exhibitions. Principles of working with artists, museums, and galleries. Museum and gallery space management. Practical training in curating art exhibitions. External studies are conducted.
derived_eng_desc1: Focuses on curatorial practices, art exhibitions, museums, and galleries, directly fitting arts and humanities.

eng_desc: The story of the Buddha has come for some to be a story of authenticity, individualism and wisdom-seeking. Yet it has not always been so. Buddhism in Thailand has followed a gamut of historical changes, from promoting monarchy through monumental architecture to modernization and meditation to, at times, being a handmaiden of military rule. It has often in Thailand been accompanied by narratives of ghosts and dark magic, as well as of tiger-defying monks and romantic tales of bodhisattvas. By stressing how Buddhism has changed in Thailand over time and place, this course aims to look critically rather than romantically or conservatively at what Buddhism has been in Thailand over the centuries, of how it has tied itself to and reflected the desires, fears and political wills of its followers.
derived_eng_desc1: Explores the history and cultural impact of Buddhism in Thailand, directly fitting arts and humanities.

eng_name: Dance Skills for Khon and Lakhon (Thai Dance Drama)
eng_desc: The subject covers the theories and practices of Thai classical dance. The origin and development of Khon-Lakhon (Thai Dance Drama), the content of which includes their connection to, politics, religion, economics, and cultural institutes in each period of Thai history. Students are trained in various dance drama forms, for example, Khon, Lakorn nai, Lakorn nok, Lakorn panthang and other dance dramas. They will analyze Thai Dance Drama in detail, as well as get basic training on their performing skills. A short scene work performance or individual research is required for the final project.
derived_eng_desc1: Covers theories and practices of Thai classical dance drama (Khon-Lakhon), including performing skills and cultural context.

eng_desc: The synopsis evolution of prehistoric, western, eastern, and Thai art, reflecting social and historical background, beliefs, aesthetic, and creativity as intellect properties to design innovation.
derived_eng_desc1: Explores the evolution of art (prehistoric, Western, Eastern, Thai), reflecting social/historical context and creativity for design innovation.

eng_desc: The use of voice in describing and expressing emotions; textual studies; character analysis; preparation before dubbing and voice acting; vocal and dubbing practices for various program types.
derived_eng_desc1: Focuses on dubbing and voice acting, including vocal practices, textual studies, and character analysis for various program types.

eng_name: Theater in Britain and the United States
eng_desc: Theater as a form of cultural expression and the relation of theater to key ideological, cultural and aesthetic debates in the United Kingdom and the United States.
derived_eng_desc1: Explores theater as cultural expression in Britain and the United States, examining its relation to ideological, cultural, and aesthetic debates.

eng_desc: Theoretical, historical, and political dimensions of film studies; basic philosophy on aesthetics, art movement, critical theories of diverse schools of thought; scopes and meanings of film criticism, both content and context; use of thinking models and tools to enable students to deeply and systematically analyze and understand the essence of film; relationship between film and social institutions; student presentations on topics such as film artists, film philosophy, politics in film, etc.
derived_eng_desc1: Explores film theory and criticism, covering historical, political, and philosophical dimensions, aesthetics, and critical analysis of film.

eng_desc: Theories and approaches in language acquisition; process of language acquisition; relationship between language and communication in various situations; contemporary issues and trends in language learning.
derived_eng_desc1: Focuses on language acquisition, communication, and language learning, aligning with languages/literature.

eng_desc: Theories and practice of advanced lighting design and installation for theatre and other types of performance.
derived_eng_desc1: Focuses on lighting design for theatre and performance, aligning with arts and performing arts.

eng_desc: Theories and practice of advanced scenic design for various types of performance. Students practice building scenery in a laboratory.
derived_eng_desc1: Focuses on scenic design and building for performance, aligning with arts and performing arts.

eng_desc: Theories and practices for paper arts and crafts with emphasis on 2-dimetional works.
derived_eng_desc1: Focuses on paper arts and crafts, directly aligning with arts and creative expression.

eng_desc: Theories and practices for paper arts and crafts with emphasis on 3-dimentional works and various paper modeling techniques.
derived_eng_desc1: Focuses on paper arts and crafts, including 3D modeling, directly aligning with arts and creative expression.

eng_desc: Theories and practices of vocal skills, such as breath control, vocal vibration, muscle command, quality voice projection, correct pronunciation of consonants and vowels, as well as interpretation of texts through vocalization.
derived_eng_desc1: Focuses on vocal skills, voice training, and oral interpretation, aligning with performing arts and creative expression.

eng_desc: Theories of theatre spaces. Types, methods, and practice in using tools and techniques for creating scenery. Basic design elements for theatre.
derived_eng_desc1: Focuses on theatre spaces, scenery creation, and design elements for theatre, aligning with performing arts.

eng_name: Principles of Textile and Apparel Design
eng_desc: Theories, concepts and elements of art and textile design, physical and psychological aspects of color and apply on the design, printing designs.
derived_eng_desc1: Focuses on textile and apparel design principles, art elements, and color, aligning with arts and creative design.

eng_desc: Theory and practice of consecutive and simultaneous interpreting in the conference interpreting context; application of language and translation theories to language interpreting; practice of referencing for specialized areas of knowledge to facilitate interpreting; practice of listening for gist and note-taking skills for consecutive interpreting and listening-deverbalizing-formulation skills for simultaneous interpreting; development and management of glossaries and reference material.
derived_eng_desc1: Focuses on theory and practice of consecutive and simultaneous interpreting, applying language and translation theories.

eng_desc: Theory and practice of stage make up for theatre and other types of performance.
derived_eng_desc1: Focuses on theory and practice of stage make-up for theatre and other performances.

eng_desc: Theory and practice of various types of dances.
derived_eng_desc1: Covers theory and practice of various types of dances, a performing art.

eng_desc: These subject covers theory and Practice of Central and Southern Performing Arts study both in acting The relationship between folk dance and society Culture, traditions, way of life, beliefs and religious rituals The development of folk dance engage in research and analysis of relevant information.
derived_eng_desc1: Covers theory and practice of Central and Southern Thai folk dances, their culture and traditions.

eng_desc: Thinking processes; presentation of ideas; skill development and application of Thai language principles for efficient translation.
derived_eng_desc1: Develops Thai language skills for communication, translation, and presentation of ideas.

eng_desc: This course aims to build on acquired proficiency at the elementary level towards achieving more fluency in listening, speaking, reading, and writing through Thai socio-cultural skills. The intermediate level introduces new vocabulary and grammar through communicative tasks and text readings, mainly using the situational-communicative methodology. Students are required to have completed Elementary Thai. At the end of the course, students are expected to be able to: conduct small talk with native speakers - read short paragraphs in Thai. converse in Thai on certain common topics
derived_eng_desc1: Aims to develop intermediate proficiency in Thai language skills: listening, speaking, reading, and writing.

eng_desc: This course aims to further develop students' skills--speaking, listening, reading, and writing-- at a more advanced level. In this course, students are expected to be able to communicate in Russian in everyday situations. (Lecture and practice 6 hours per week)
derived_eng_desc1: Develops advanced Russian language skills in speaking, listening, reading, and writing for everyday communication.

eng_desc: This course covers further study of basic grammar from Business Communication in Japanese 2. Practice listening, speaking, reading, writing Japanese sentences using vocabularies in daily life conversation, practicing verb conjugation and conversation related to business dealings, introducing the team, recommending products, trading using more complex sentences and learning culture communicating with the Japanese.
derived_eng_desc1: Focuses on Japanese language skills, business communication, and Japanese culture.

eng_desc: This course covers the study of sound system, pronunciation practice, character writing Hiragana, Katagana and Kanji, basic grammar and vocabulary enabling students to make basic sentences used in daily life and basic business situations : introducing oneself, making appointment, trading, travelling and learning culture communicating with the Japanese.
derived_eng_desc1: Covers Japanese language fundamentals, business communication, and cultural aspects.

eng_desc: This course emphasizes fundamental language skills of listening, speaking, reading, and writing through Thai culture. The students are not required to have prior knowledge of the Thai language. At the end of the course, the students are expected to be able to: converse in Thai with a basic structure read non-complex words and sentences
derived_eng_desc1: Emphasizes fundamental Thai language skills and Thai culture.

eng_desc: This course examines the principles and fundamental theories of Thai Dance, as well as providing students with demonstrations of standard Thai Dance for further learning. Students will be introduced to the basic elements of music, the art of music, stylistic characteristics and a brief overview of the history of Western and Southeast Asian classical music, folk music, and period music. Students will develop their capacity to understand and appreciate the place of music in society.
derived_eng_desc1: Explores principles and theories of Thai dance and music, including history and cultural place.

eng_desc: This course fits into the vision of Group T that engineers have a higher purpose: to develop people and to improve conditions for humankind. In order to reach this goal students need to have a holistic vision on engineering and they have to become aware of the interplay between technology and society. Moreover, the engineer of the future will be situated in a globalised world in which he/she will have to live, work and interact with people of many different cultures and religious traditions. Religions have a major impact on how people feel and behave and on what they consider important in their lives. As such, it is also an important factor in how they will respond to new technologies. Moreover, technology as such raises important religious and spiritual issues. This course on Religions wishes to help students in engineering technology understand the impact of religions on the daily life of people and their willingness to adopt new technologies. It also wishes to confront them with a plurality of religious perspectives on science, technology and sustainability, and show them how technology challenges religion. Furthermore, the course also intends to help students clarify their own stance vis-à-vis religion and how religious traditions may inspire them in deepening and formulating their call as engineers in the society of the future. Learning Outcomes: G2: Communication with engineers and non-engineers G3: Critical thinking Aims: Students are able to indicate the core elements of a number of the major religions, with a special focus on those elements that will be important for their future interaction with adherents of these religions (G3) Students are able to assess how religious views and sensibilities may impact the adoption and success of new technologies (G3) Students are able to tell about the diversity of views and perspectives on science, technology and sustainability that exist among and within the religions (G3) Students are able to identify religious and spiritual issues raised by technology, to explain how technology challenges the religions and to formulate answers to the question of what religion in dialogue with technology teach us about what it means to be human (G3) Students are able to reflect on religious and spiritual issues in the context of their field of study, they are able to take a stance on these matters in a substantiated way, and to enter into dialogue with fellow students on them (G2, G3) Students are able to explain how they are challenged by a confrontation with a number of the major religious traditions (G3) Students are able to indicate the importance of religion and world views, also in connection with their own life, and they are able to reflect critically on their own ideological prejudices and presuppositions (G3) Students are able to explain their responsibility and their call as engineers in the society of the future, and they are able to clarify in which way religious traditions inspire them when doing this (G3)
derived_eng_desc1: Explores major religions, their impact on society, technology, and sustainability, and spiritual issues.

eng_desc: This course introduces students to the power of creativity and creative thinking, as a key component of a 21st century skillset. This includes a wide range of techniques from across the creative industries, exploring both internal drivers and external tools for creative thought and action. Students learn hands-on approaches for harnessing the imagination, exploring new possibilities for relating to and being in the World. At the same time, students negotiate the limits and potentials of global intersections, with a focus on issues of sustainability and ecology.
derived_eng_desc1: Focuses on creativity, creative thinking, and creative industries, aligning with cultural and creative expression.

eng_desc: This course involves further study of German grammar and business communication following on from Business Communication in German 1, as well as basic reading and writing and building economics and business related vocabulary by means of printed matter and the internet. This should allow students to understand daily lifestyles and viewpoints of Germans to a reasonable extent.
derived_eng_desc1: Focuses on German language, grammar, and cultural understanding, even with a business context.

eng_desc: This course involves further study of basic grammar from Business Communication in Japanese 1. Practice listening, speaking, reading and forming basic sentences using daily life vocabularies and making conversation related to self introduction, making appointment, recommending products, trading, travelling and learning culture communicating with the Japanese.
derived_eng_desc1: Focuses on Japanese language skills, grammar, and cultural communication.

eng_desc: This course involves further study of basic grammar from Business Communication in Japanese 3. Practice listening, speaking, reading, writing Japanese sentences using daily – life vocabularies. Practice verb conjugation, polite language in noble form (keigo) and humble form (kensongo), conversations related to business dealings in formal situations using appropriate noble (keigo) and humble (kensongo) verb forms and learning culture communicating with the Japanese. After completing Business Communication in Japanese 1 4, students will have basic Japanese proficiency and be able to take the Level 4 Proficiency Test.
derived_eng_desc1: Focuses on advanced Japanese language proficiency, grammar, and cultural nuances for communication.

eng_name: Man and Arts: Visual Art, Music and Performing Arts
eng_desc: This course is a study of art in relation to its function and the development of people, society and environment by focusing on various creative works, such as visual arts, music and performing arts, depicting the culture and perception of mankind. The course also aims to instill learners with real awareness of art values through personal experience, and also the appreciation of the aesthetic values of creative works. An emphasis is placed upon the influence of art on Thai values and the Thai way of life.
derived_eng_desc1: Explicitly studies visual art, music, performing arts, and their cultural impact.

eng_desc: This course is aimed at upper intermediate-level students or above and emphasizes the development of reading and writing skills through the analysis of a wide variety of texts. Students will learn to read longer and more abstract writing, advertisements from newspapers, and articles from magazines and webpage. Students will learn more expressions, figures of speech, higher level grammar, and hierarchical pronouns. Writing will move from descriptive to explanatory. Students are required to have completed Upper-Intermediate Thai. Course Objectives At the end of the course, students are expected to be able to: read and analyze passages from various texts. write paragraphs in Thai using standard Thai grammar. make an impromptu oral presentation in Thai
derived_eng_desc1: Focuses on advanced Thai language skills, grammar, reading, and writing.

eng_desc: This course is designed to enhance students' competence in writing Thai. This course is for students who have learned the fundamentals of Thai composition sufficiently to progress to a more sophisticated level. Students who have not completed Advanced Thai must be assessed by the instructor first. Students must be able to read and write Thai at a good level (understand the use of complex Thai structures, have a wide variety of vocabulary, and understand the differences in word usage in different contexts). At the end of the course, the students are expected to be able to: - Write argumentative essays and opinion pieces that are 300-500 words long.
derived_eng_desc1: Enhances advanced writing competence in the Thai language, focusing on composition and essays.

eng_desc: This course is designed to focus on reading and comprehension. And is designed for those with an advanced knowledge of Thai. Students who have not completed Advanced Thai must be assessed by the instructor first. Students must be able to read and write Thai at a good level (understand the use of complex Thai structures, have a variety of vocabulary, and understand the differences in word usage in different contexts). The learning focuses more on understanding Thai language in various contexts and analyzing the text. The texts selected will comprise short stories and poetry or passages covering topics such as politics, history, science, technology medicine, and more. The course will help students become more proficient with nuanced/implied meanings, bolster vocabulary and acquire familiarity with various literary devices. At the end of the course, students are expected to be able to: - Read and understand advanced texts - Write summaries and reviews using persuasive arguments in Thai
derived_eng_desc1: Develops advanced reading and comprehension skills in Thai, analyzing various texts and literary devices.

eng_desc: This course is for learners who want to learn basic translation, both translations from Thai to English and translation from English to Thai. Students must have sufficient basic knowledge of Thai language. Students who have not completed Advanced Thai must be assessed by the instructor first and must also have a good level of English language proficiency. Materials range from magazine articles, to poetry, to novels and academic texts. Course Objectives At the end of the course, the students are expected to be able to: Understand that usage of Thai language differs depending on the context Write translations from Thai to English and English to Thai
derived_eng_desc1: Introduces basic translation skills between Thai and English, covering various text types.

eng_desc: This course is for students who want to learn colloquial Thai (the form they will hear most) from contemporary multimedia, such as movies, series, podcasts, songs, newspapers, websites, etc. Students must have a good level of conversational Thai especially in terms of listening and speaking. Students who have not studied Advanced Thai must be assessed by the instructor first. Speaking and listening skills are the focus of this course. At the end of the course, students are expected to be able to: Understand that usage of Thai is adjusted in different contexts Understand contemporary, colloquial Thai Use colloquial Thai in appropriate contexts with a high degree of fluency and confidence
derived_eng_desc1: Teaches colloquial Thai through popular media, focusing on listening and speaking skills.

eng_desc: This course offers a forum for examining selected fundamental issues in legal theories and specific issues of current interest in philosophy of law. For the seminal purposes, a list of issues will be published in each semester.
derived_eng_desc1: Examines fundamental issues in legal theories and philosophy of law, aligning with arts and humanities.

eng_desc: This course provides a flexible approach to grammar instruction and integrates the study of new structures (form) with information on how to use them and what they mean (function). Comprehensive grammar coverage ensures a thorough and effective presentation of all basic structures. Extensive practice guides students to accurate production and fluent use of new grammar. Short writing assignments incorporate grammar into step-by-step tasks for a variety of writing purposes, such as narrating and describing. There is also a focus on real-world listening skills.
derived_eng_desc1: Focuses on English grammar, writing, and listening skills, aligning with language studies.

eng_desc: This course provides a study, in a comparative dimension, of concepts and principles of particular importance in the French and Thai legal systems. In this connection, emphasis is placed on practice in reading, translation and drafting contracts in French.
derived_eng_desc1: Focuses on French legal terminology, translation, and drafting contracts in French, combining law and language.

eng_desc: This course provides a study, in a comparative dimension, of concepts and principles of particular importance in the German and Thai legal systems. In this connection, emphasis is placed on practice in reading, translation and drafting contracts in German.
derived_eng_desc1: Focuses on German legal terminology, translation, and drafting contracts in German, combining law and language.

eng_desc: This course specializes in the principles of textile design as they relate to home furnishing fabrication, wall coverings, and other interior related products. In addition to introduction to perspective drawing for interior design. Field trips are included.
derived_eng_desc1: Specializes in textile design, home furnishing, interior design, and related product fabrication.

eng_desc: This course specializes in the principles of textile design as they relate to home furnishing fabrication, wall coverings, and other interior related products. In addition to introduction to perspective drawing for interior design. Field trips are included.
derived_eng_desc1: Specializes in textile design, home furnishing, interior design, and related product fabrication.

eng_desc: This course takes students on a journey through successive human occupations in the Chao Phraya River basin, from a pre-Tai period to early Tai migrations, Sukhothai, Ayutthaya and Bangkok, providing students with an essential foundation to the understanding of modern-day Thailand. This course not only introduces students to the history of Thailand but also to the discipline of history itself. In doing so, students will understand that while facts exist, what facts are selected and how they are interpreted will depend on the historian and his or her sponsors. Students will appreciate the varieties of Thai history, moving beyond the merely political to social and cultural history of Thai (and Tai) speaking-peoples and how they have interacted with their neighbours. By the end of the course students will have improved their skills in critical thinking, data analysis, researching via digital means, argumentative reasoning and persuasive writing. This course introduces students to the intellectual and physical resources required for life-long learning about history and the ways in which history informs the present.
derived_eng_desc1: Explores Thai history, from early periods to modern-day, including social and cultural aspects.

eng_name: Great Books: Human Intellectual Development through Key Texts
eng_desc: This course, based on well-regarded core curriculum courses at institutions such as Columbia University and the University of Chicago, aims to give students a grounding in intellectual and scientific history by way of studying great books. The reading list includes classic works in philosophy, literature, history, religion, economics and the history of science, from Greek classics and Sanskrit epics to Enlightenment-period masterpieces. The course will develop students' understanding of human intellectual history across regions as well as aiming to enhance critical thinking and academic reading and writing skills.
derived_eng_desc1: Studies great books in philosophy, literature, history, religion, and science to understand human intellectual development.

eng_desc: This project introduces basic field research methodology and their own interest focusing on the learning of the lifestyle, customs, traditions, as well as local folk arts that reflect the long history, beliefs, folklore and the techniques of cultural transmission to new generations which preserve to the present. The materials gained from the field trip are expected to be inspirational to the following contemporary creative art project of the students, while at the same time paying respect to the original source.
derived_eng_desc1: Focuses on field research, local folk arts, and contemporary creative art projects, aligning with arts and design.

eng_name: Practice in English for Fine and Applied Arts 1
eng_desc: This subject aims to implement English usage skills which are relevant to each artistic discipline. These skills include reading, writing, and conversation. The selected topics concern various aspects of culture.
derived_eng_desc1: Focuses on English skills relevant to fine and applied arts and culture, aligning with arts and humanities.

eng_name: Religions and Philosophies of Thailand: Origins and Contemporary Issues
eng_desc: While Thailand is often thought of as a Buddhist country, it in fact contains much religious diversity. This course acts as a broad introduction to the study of major religions such as Buddhism, Christianity, Islam as well as folk or popular religion in Thailand. As well as covering the theory of the study of religions, this course looks at how these religions continue to play vital roles in shaping Thai society and politics in the present day. By the end of the course students will have improved their skills in critical thinking, data analysis, researching via digital means, argumentative reasoning, persuasive writing, presentation skills and rhetoric using a wide variety of media. The course encourages students to recognize and critically engage with alternative values.
derived_eng_desc1: Introduces major religions and philosophies in Thailand, their origins, and their contemporary roles in shaping society and politics.

eng_name: Arts and Literature of Southeast Asia
eng_desc: Yet this region of what is now multiple nation-states was once far more interlinked and inter-influencing. This is reflected in the great variety of classical literature and art shared across the region. To give one example, Adrian Vickers has described the region as a Panji-civilization, based on the immense popularity of that now largely-forgotten romancing, island-conquering protagonist. This course will move beyond the often-artificial boundaries of language and nation-state to explore the wealth of shared culture and history in the region. By the end of the course students will have improved their skills in critical thinking, data analysis, researching via digital means, argumentative reasoning, persuasive writing, presentation skills and rhetoric using a wide variety of media.
derived_eng_desc1: Explores the classical literature, art, shared culture, and history of Southeast Asia across national boundaries.

eng_desc: A study of climate change and major disasters such as earthquakes, tsunamis,floods, landslides, fire, terrorism and nuclear accidents; their socio-economic impact on thewell-being of people and communities at the national, regional and global levels; an analysis ofhazards and risks; and the roles and responsibilities of international communities, state andprivate agencies in responding to the impact of climate change and disasters and recoverywork. Various case studies are examined and students develop digital innovation concept proposals that could address social and sustainability challenges.
derived_eng_desc1: Examines digital technologies for social innovation, addressing social and sustainability challenges.

eng_name: Special Topic in Education and Society

derived_eng_desc1: Analyzes social, political, economic, and cultural implications of urban plans and governance, fitting social sciences.

derived_eng_desc1: Studies international organizations and regimes, focusing on their role in solving global social, economic, and political problems.

derived_eng_desc1: Examines the impact of technology on cultural systems and anthropological aspects, using historical and archaeological evidence.

eng_desc: The concept and meaning of good governance. Basic principles for building good governance. Good command in the Thai context. Sustainability governance of sustainable development relationship construction with stakeholders. Driving good governance in public and private management. A case study of good governance for sustainable development.
derived_eng_desc1: Explores good governance concepts, principles, and sustainable development in public and private management.

eng_desc: The contemporary issues in ASEAN countries. Study various aspects of the overall ASEAN or each country's economy i. e. socio-economic issues, politics, businesses, trade and investment, economic development, finance, etc. Roles of regional organizations, economic interconnection across countries, and linkages with the Thai economy. The learning methods are the active and problem-based learning with some experienced guest speakers, discussion, and field trips visiting public and/or private organization(s) in Thailand and another ASEAN member country, according to the lecturer's announcement.
derived_eng_desc1: Examines socio-economic, political, business, trade, and financial issues in ASEAN countries and regional organizations.

eng_name: Residential Estate Development and Community Development
eng_desc: The context of various elements of rural society, semi-urban society and urban society of Thailand. And analyse social change processes, problems and impacts of national development in accordance with government policies such as National Economic and Social Development Plan Leading to the use of knowledge in social science, humanities and architecture to analyse problems, plan and propose guidelines for development at various levels to result in an integrated development including physical, economic, social, cultural and environment approach.
derived_eng_desc1: Analyzes social change, national development impacts on rural/urban societies, using social science, humanities, and architecture for integrated community development.

eng_desc: The course explores theories and concepts in sociology and state agencies related to urban development. Social group, civil society and participation in urban policy and planning will be discussed. Governmental structure of central, regional and local administration, including public administration, state's role, power and duty in urban policy and planning and public services provision will be explored.
derived_eng_desc1: Explores sociology and state agencies related to urban development, focusing on social groups, civil society, and public administration in urban planning.

eng_desc: The course introduces students to the various transnational flows, such as human flows (migration, asylum seeking), data and information flows (misinformation, disinformation, malinfornation, etc.), flows of pathogens as well as the larger impact of globalization on human, animal and environmental health (Global Health, One Health, Planetary Health), etc. It exposes students to the complex nature of globalization and equips them with tools and techniques to apprehend that complexity. The course also seeks the linkages between that understanding of globalization with the development of the relevant 21st century skills to address, and collectively solve, “wicked problems".
derived_eng_desc1: Focuses on globalization, human/data flows, and societal impacts, aligning with social sciences.

eng_name: Artificial Intelligence Ethics for Leader of the Future
eng_desc: The course presents an introduction to Al, covering its definition, principles, applications, and the advantages and disadvantages. Students will explore the broader impacts of Al on the economy, society, and environment. In addition, it introduces trustworthy Al concept, focusing on transparency, fairness, accountability, and robustness, emphasizing the creation of ethical Al systems. Finally, students will delve into Al ethics, applying ethical theories to real-world scenarios through case studies and discussions to understand the benefits and risks of Al.
derived_eng_desc1: Focuses on AI ethics, societal impacts, and trustworthy AI concepts, aligning with social sciences.

eng_desc: The course will introduce students to the intellectual foundations of and debates on the concept of human security; and the various aspects of human security such as: political, economic, environmental, food, health, personal, and community security; as well how forces and processes of globalization have an impact on aspects of human security.
derived_eng_desc1: Introduces human security, covering political, economic, environmental, and social aspects of globalization.

eng_desc: The definition of impact; concepts, theories of impact evaluation; historical development of impact evaluation; the significance of impact evaluation and sustainable development; economics, environment, health, and social dimensions of impact evaluation; related types and evaluation models; the development of theory of change, results chain, and impact evaluation questions; the design of evaluation process; impact evaluation of social programs; utilization of evaluation results; strengths and weaknesses of impact evaluation; the ethical consideration regarding evaluation; criticism of impact evaluation's case studies.
derived_eng_desc1: Focuses on impact evaluation concepts, theories, and models across economic, social, and environmental dimensions.

eng_desc: The development and concepts of socio-cultural resource management at national and international levels. The course focuses on the role of government agencies, organizations and other sectors in socio-cultural resource management; as well as the impacts of development and management.
derived_eng_desc1: Focuses on socio-cultural resource management, including roles of agencies and development impacts.

eng_desc: The development of citizenship attitudes in a self-reliant democracy in solving social problems; Learn how to take self action to solve problems in society by designing the learning process and evaluation in collaboration with instructor.
derived_eng_desc1: Focuses on developing citizenship attitudes and solving social problems in a democracy.

derived_eng_desc1: Focuses on field immersion, integrating social skills and sustainability knowledge into community practice, problem analysis, and development.

derived_eng_desc1: Focuses on psychological skills training and techniques for athletes, aligning with social and behavioural sciences.

eng_desc: The importance and benefits of mental skills training for athletes. Process of the mental skills training for athletes for examples, goal setting, self talk and self - thought, imagery, breathing control and muscle relaxation. Designing a mental training plan for athletes.
derived_eng_desc1: Focuses on mental skills training for athletes, including psychological techniques, aligning with social sciences.

eng_desc: The importance of the economy's industrial sector. Relationship between the industrial sector and other sectors, on the domestic and international level. Studying market structure, conduct, and competitiveness of the industrial sector. Government policy, the legal system, and their effects on industrial development.
derived_eng_desc1: Focuses on industrial economics, market structure, government policy, and industrial development, aligning with social sciences.

eng_desc: The meaning, principles, philosophy, ideology and choices of development from the various schools of thought in social studies. The course considers the relationship between economic, social, cultural, political, physical factors that affect development; Development strategies and the impacts of development.
derived_eng_desc1: Focuses on development concepts, theories, and factors from social studies, aligning with social sciences.

eng_desc: The origin of human rights concept; the formation of human rights movements and its implication in 21st century; debates on human rights. Human rights as the foundation of rights to data and rights with relation to the digital technology.
derived_eng_desc1: Covers human rights concepts, movements, and their implications in the digital era, fitting social sciences.

eng_desc: The role of agriculture in economic development. Structure and structural change of the agricultural economy. Production, market, and price of agricultural products. Agricultural institutions. The relationship between agriculture and natural resource and environmental problems. Agricultural development policies in Thailand.
derived_eng_desc1: Focuses on the economic aspects of agriculture, including markets, prices, and policies, aligning with social sciences.

eng_desc: The role of religion towards state; relations between religion and political movements; contemporary debates on religion-state relations.
derived_eng_desc1: Examines the relationship between religion and politics, including state relations and political movements, aligning with social sciences.

eng_desc: The role of transportation in the domestic and international economy. How transportation affects the location of businesses and production sites. Criteria and economic reasons for transportation pricing. Private and social costs related to transportation. How urban transportation is affected by expansion. Problems and policies related to investment in urban transportation.
derived_eng_desc1: Analyzes the economic aspects of transportation, including pricing, costs, and policies, aligning with social sciences.

eng_desc: The role, concept and the relationship between Public Administration and International Development. A study of the development and influence of international development approach that directly and indirectly impacts on central, regional, and local government administration. The course focuses on analysing the application of international development policy to practice at the national level. The focus is also on enhancing the skills of a public administration practitioner who studies holistic problems from a national level to International level, as well as problem management with applied interdisciplinary knowledge.
derived_eng_desc1: Studies public administration, international development, government policy, and problem management, aligning with social sciences.

eng_desc: The roles of physiology, instinct, learning, and cognition in motivation and emotion; related theories of motivation and emotion for explaining behavior.
derived_eng_desc1: Explores theories of motivation, emotion, and behavior, drawing from psychology and social sciences.

derived_eng_desc1: Focuses on audience analysis using theories from communication, psychology, and marketing to understand media users.

derived_eng_desc1: Focuses on econometrics, including statistical models for economic data, aligning with social sciences.

eng_name: Critical Perspectives on Design and Innovation
eng_desc: This course critically investigates the role of design and innovation in social intervention programs. In recent years, the language of design and innovation has been appropriated in generating solution for social problems, from poverty to community development. This course provides critical perspectives and analytical toolkits for such interventions. In particular, we question the efficacy of design as a tool for social change, and the 'solutionism'in which social issues are framed as ‘problem' to be solved. In addition, we interrogate the social mission of digital techs and big businesses and the impact they are creating for society.
derived_eng_desc1: Investigates design and innovation in social intervention programs and their impact on society.

eng_desc: This course endeavors to provide an account of historical backgrounds and current issues surrounding political parties, electoral systems and agencies in charge of elections in Thailand. With regard to political parties, this course places particular emphasis on structures and roles of political parties under legislation currently in force. As far as legislation on elections, this course seeks to explore strengths and shortcomings found in the electoral systems and the electoral agency under current legislation and approaches to revise such legislation.
derived_eng_desc1: Covers political parties, electoral law, and electoral systems, aligning with politics.

eng_name: Thai Sociolinguistics: Languages, Society and Meaning
eng_desc: This course examines the history and development of the Central Thai language, its origins among the Tai language families of Southern China, contemporary related regional dialects, and its relationship with neighbouring Southeast Asian languages, such as Khmer and Mon. The course explores the use of contemporary Thai language and its dialects in contexts where speakers seek to determine social or speech group differentiation, the phenomenon of codes and code switching, register, sociolect and accent, how Thai has been taught to Thai citizens and foreigners and issues of national identity and politicisation. This course provides students of Thai Studies with a clearer understanding of contemporary Thai cultural and social life. By the end of the course students will have improved their skills in critical thinking, data analysis, researching via digital means, argumentative reasoning, persuasive writing, presentation skills and rhetoric using a wide variety of media. This course further develops understanding and use of the fundamentals of effective communication. Students are provided with the opportunity to develop their skills in joint projects working in pairs and in groups. It allows students to design and execute their own research projects.
derived_eng_desc1: Examines Thai sociolinguistics, language development, social differentiation, and cultural aspects.

eng_name: Seminar on Law and State Policy on Women
eng_desc: This course explores the evolution of the change of women's legal status as well as changes in State's policies and mechanisms vis-à-vis women. The study is centered on the development of modern society as from the major change of the government regime in 1932 up to present, with analysis of economic, social, political and cultural factors in each epoch leading to revision and adaptation of State's policies, legal reform and the organisation of the State organs with a view to greater equality for women. Developments in other jurisdictions will be compared and contrasted with international standards established in international instruments of the United Nations e.g. the United Nations Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women.
derived_eng_desc1: Examines law and state policy on women, focusing on legal status, equality, and social factors.

eng_desc: This course explores the interrelationships between gender and technology and the ways in which culture and society shape the design and use of technology and vice versa. We will look at gender-technology relations, including reproductive technologies, the gendering of technological artefacts, gendered roles and stereotypes, and gender dynamics in the digital age, using empirical case studies and theoretical approaches from gender, science, and technology studies. Students will identify and analyse contemporary global issues relating to gender and technology and apply a critical perspective. One of these issues pertains to work and the ways in which new technologies (e.g., digitalization, Al) are changing the way work gets done, how people are adapting to this fast-changing world of work in the 21 st century, and the gender implications of technology on work: Are women's jobs at risk of being displaced/replaced by technology? Is technological change closing or widening the gender gap? are some questions raised by a recent publication on, ‘Gender, Technology, and the Future of Work.'
derived_eng_desc1: Explores interrelationships between gender and technology, focusing on social, cultural, and work impacts.

eng_name: Introduction to Environmental Policy and Planning
eng_desc: This course focuses on national environmental and energy policy-making; environmental ethics; the techniques of environmental analysis; and strategies for collaborative environmental decision-making. The primary objective of the course is to help students formulate a personal theory of environmental planning practice. The course is taught comparatively, with constant references to examples from around the world. The national environmental and energy policy-making, environmental ethics, the techniques of environmental analysis, and strategies for collaborative environmental decision making. Strengths and weaknesses of key techniques of environmental analysis like cost-benefit analysis, environmental impact assessment, modelling and simulation, sustainability analysis, and risk assessment. Collaborative decision-making and dispute resolution techniques as they are used in the practice of environmental and energy facility planning.
derived_eng_desc1: Focuses on environmental and energy policy-making, planning, ethics, and analytical techniques for sustainable decision-making.

eng_desc: This course focusses on the nature and analysis of organisations in the civil societysector; motivations to work emphasising non-fiscal incentives; laws concerning non-profitorganisations; fund raising and management of human resources and other components in adevelopment and social welfare organisation. It also explores the typology of civil societyorganisations, the politics and development of civil society organisations, as well as the socialrole and impact of civil society organisations on sustainably solving social problems andgovernment-civil society relationships.
derived_eng_desc1: Focuses on civil society organizations, their management, development, social role, and impact on social problems.

eng_desc: This course gives an account of the general principles of microeconomics and macroeconomics. In microeconomics part, topics cover demand for and supply of goods, consumer behavior, production and costs, structure and behavior of production units under perfectly and imperfectly competitive markets, the concept of market failures and the role of government intervention, applications of economics to understand and analyze the law and legal system. In macroeconomics part, topics cover objectives and problems in macroeconomic, national income determination, money and banking system, introduction to fiscal and monetary policies used for economic stabilization, the application of economic indices to analyze the economic situation.
derived_eng_desc1: Introduces microeconomics and macroeconomics principles, including market failures, government intervention, and economic policies.

eng_name: Introduction to Area Studies and Its Methodology
eng_desc: This course introduces area studies as a practical interdisciplinary approach to the study of regions and countries of the world. The course provides the student with an awareness of what the study of areas of the world entails and the theoretical and methodological discussions of global phenomena. The course focuses on how our understanding of regions and countries can be enhanced through social sciences and humanities perspectives and how knowledge of language, history and culture constitutes the basis of area studies.
derived_eng_desc1: Introduces interdisciplinary area studies, focusing on regions, countries, global phenomena, social sciences, and humanities.

eng_desc: This course provides an in-depth analysis and critique of digital transformationand in particular the rapid development of digital technologies, the digital economy and e-government, big data and their impact on social issues and social policy in Thailand, theSoutheast Asian region and other parts of the world. Rights, inequality, individual identity andprivacy affected by the digital divide and digital literacy and new social measures and policydirections will also be investigated.
derived_eng_desc1: Analyzes digital transformation, technologies, and their impact on social issues, policy, rights, and inequality.

eng_desc: This course seeks to go beyond such fantasies to examine historical and contemporary forms of gender and eroticism. Through film, literature and contemporary media we will examine the interpretation of gender roles, explore representations of intimate relationships and query debates on homosexuality and transgender issues. By the end of the course students will have improved their skills in critical thinking, data analysis, researching via digital means, argumentative reasoning, persuasive writing, presentation skills and rhetoric using a wide variety of media. The course encourages students to recognize and critically engage with alternative values.
derived_eng_desc1: Examines gender and sexuality, gender roles, and related social issues through a social science lens.

eng_desc: This course will discuss the theories and approaches to conflict resolution based oncase studies from specific countries. It will also include review of the approaches andmethodology of negotiations and mediation as part of conflict resolution initiatives. Relevantinternational, regional and national conventions and policy frameworks that have beendeveloped for conflict resolution will also be included in this course.
derived_eng_desc1: Discusses theories and approaches to negotiation and conflict resolution, including international policy frameworks.

eng_name: Seminar on Problems in Political Philosophy
eng_desc: This module studies about the problems in political philosophy such as what is power, what is politics, what is justice, what is the good life and what is a good political society like by examining the works of one of the great political thinkers from either the Greek, Roman, Medieval, Renaissance or the Enlightenment period up until Nietzsche. This module selects some of the important works of the chosen thinker for detailed textual analysis whilst giving importance to A) the philosophical setting before the time of the chosen thinker, B) the historical context both before and during the time of the chosen thinker and C) the contribution that his/her ideas have towards political thought in subsequent periods. All this also serves to point out the fundamental differences between “political philosophy” and “political theory”.
derived_eng_desc1: Examines problems in political philosophy, power, justice, and political thinkers, aligning with social sciences and politics.

eng_desc: This seminar deals with the characteristics and problems unique to Thai political concepts by selecting to consider issues relating to cultural influences leading to Thai political concepts; the influence of Western political concepts on Thai political thought and political thought of prominent Thai philosophers from the past to the present.
derived_eng_desc1: Examines Thai political concepts, cultural influences, and political thought of philosophers, aligning with social sciences.

eng_desc: Through engagement with sociological and anthropological theory, this course examines the development of digital technologies and how their use is reshaping society and producing unintended consequences. It asks how certain social values are embedded in digital technologies and how those values are accepted and resisted. It examines the impact of digital technologies on society, culture, politics and the economy. It explores how digital inequalities and exclusion could mitigate and amplify social, political and inequalities. The course facilitates an understanding of the distinction between empowering technologies and control technologies. It considers the development of digital infrastructure, the growth of the internet and social media, digital platforms, and frontier technologies such as IoT, Al, digital surveillance, the metaverse and blockchain.
derived_eng_desc1: Examines the development and societal impact of digital technologies on culture, politics, and economy, aligning with social sciences.

eng_name: Projects Development for Social Work Education
eng_desc: To study principles and methods of project development for social work education, in coordination withlearners, schools, families, communities and external resources. Develop plans and projects on social workeducation suitable in accordance with the needs of in-school and out-of school learners under the schooland community context, to create systemative problem solving and prevention.
derived_eng_desc1: Focuses on project development for social work education, community problem-solving, aligning with social sciences.

eng_desc: To study the development of world societies from 1500 A.D. to the present. An emphasis is placed upon the relationship of economy, political system, administration, society, culture, science and technology, leading to modern world changes.
derived_eng_desc1: Studies the development of modern world societies, including economy, politics, society, and culture.

eng_desc: Traditional and online research methods, basic data science tools and techniques for strategic planning, evaluation and measurements of corporate communication functions including image and reputation management, stakeholder relationship management, marketing and brand communication.
derived_eng_desc1: Focuses on research, data intelligence, and corporate communication.

derived_eng_desc1: Focuses on natural resource management, sustainable development, and related political, social, and economic policies.

derived_eng_desc1: Focuses on public goods, services, government roles, and social innovation for effective public service delivery.

Field trip excursion is necessary for additional experience.

derived_eng_desc1: Examines family life cycles, social change impacts on families, diverse family forms, and social work interventions for family and community strength.

eng_desc: Focuses mainly on four aspects: the history of overseas Chinese, the economic and political status of overseas Chinese in local region, the local government's policies towards overseas Chinese population, and degree of assimilation of overseas Chinese with the locals and their relationships. Comparative analysis will be used to analyze overseas Chinese communities in different countries, different regions.
derived_eng_desc1: Studies the history, economic, political, and social aspects of overseas Chinese communities and their assimilation.

derived_eng_desc1: Examines urban policy, management, and development, analyzing political, economic, and social aspects, including urban planning and social services.

eng_name: Foundation of Social Sciences and Health
eng_desc: Meaning of health and illness; illness and health systems as cultural and social phenomena; alternative medicine; social organization; socialization, social behavior social relations; social stratification related to health; social determinants of health; psychological concepts to predict health behavior; personality and health; tools in applied economics for the explanations of health services system; efficiency, equity and social justice of health services allocation; analysis of health and health care problem related to social changes.
derived_eng_desc1: Examines health and illness from social science perspectives, including cultural, social, psychological, and economic factors influencing health systems.

eng_desc: Role and significance of money in an economy; financial assets; financial markets and financial institutions; monetary theory and policy; global financial system and international monetary policies; exchange rate system; roles of international monetary institutions; discussion on current issues in monetary economics
derived_eng_desc1: Examines the economics of money, financial markets, monetary theory, policy, and the global financial system.

eng_desc: The use of cultural tools to create soft power in the context of international relations and economics. Analyzing case studies of countries successful in cultural diplomacy, such as the United States and South Korea.
